bibliographic.title: Strings Attached
bibliographic.author: Crepusucl
bibliographic.description:
Strings Attached explores complex relationship dynamics, psychological tension, and mature themes.


WARNING: You must be at least 18 years old to play this game.

A week in paradise built on secrets.

You’ve just landed in the sun-drenched hills of Spain for what was supposed to be a lavish family getaway. A sprawling luxury villa, private pools, and a chance to finally connect with your father’s new girlfriend and her breathtaking daughter. But the moment your bags hit the marble floor, the idyllic vacation begins to fracture.

Beneath the surface of lazy afternoons and expensive wine, a dangerous psychological game is unfolding. You start noticing the slips—a predatory glance held a second too long, a casual touch that crosses the line, a whispered invitation that sounds like a trap. Two women seem to be working the same illicit angle from different directions, father is completely blind to all of it, and maybe so are you.

Every conversation is a negotiation. Every boundary you push either drags you deeper into their seductive snare, or jeopardizes the one person in the house who actually has your back: your lifelong best friend.

Will you maintain your discipline? Or will the heat of the Mediterranean break you?

Features:
  • Choices That Bite: A deep, branching narrative where every decision alters the psychological power dynamics, shifts your relationships, and dictates your ultimate fate.
  • Visceral, Atmosphere-Driven Writing: Experience slow-burn tension. A story built on heavy subtext, agonizing restraint, and the explosive space between what is said and what is meant.
  • Dynamic Relationship Tracking: Navigate a cast of sharp, weaponized personalities. Keep a watchful eye on your Friendship, Tension, and Frustration—every glance, argument, and surrender shifts the scales in real-time.
  • Character Customization: Shape your protagonist's physical appearance and social traits at the start to alter how the women in the house react to you.
  • Dual Perspectives: Finish the main narrative, then flip the board. Replay the entire story from Natalie's calculating point of view and see everything on from the very beginning
